rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance (source of income and other tenant-selection limits)
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in renting housing based on protected categories, including source of income (Section 8 and public benefits). Any tenant-selection standard must be reasonable and applied equally and uniformly to all applicants, such as ability to pay rent and care for the apartment.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8) is a protected category; uniform, reasonable selection standards only
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.penalty: Civil fines of up to $300 per violation, plus injunctive relief, damages and other relief after a hearing.

parsed.doc_summary: Cambridge Human Rights Commission page describing the Fair Housing Ordinance (ch. 14.04): protected categories including source of income/Section 8, uniform reasonable tenant-selection standards, owner-occupied 2-family exemption, and a $300 per-violation fine. It states nothing on rent control, eviction, deposits, fees or algorithmic pricing.
